title: Deep-learning-guided cell-free screening identifies antimicrobial peptides
summary: Generative and predictive deep-learning models proposed and prioritized peptide sequences for cell-free synthesis and screening. The authors report 30 functional antimicrobial peptides among 500 candidates tested across five design–build–test rounds. The assay tested peptides in unpurified cell-free mixtures, a limitation for interpreting activity and potency. The reported effects do not establish clinical efficacy or antibiotic approval.
ai_technology: Variational autoencoders; convolutional and recurrent neural-network regressors
organization: Max Planck Institute for Terrestrial Microbiology; Goethe University Frankfurt; Philipps University of Marburg

evidence.tested: 500 model-prioritized candidates were produced and screened; 30 showed functional antimicrobial activity in the reported assays.
evidence.unknown: Unpurified CFPS assay mixtures, animal/human efficacy and independent replication limit interpretation.
evidence.ai_role: Generative models proposed peptide sequences and learned regressors prioritized candidates before cell-free synthesis and activity tests.

source_review.scope: Primary PubMed record, abstract and figure captions; indexed full-text results for assay conditions.
